# 005: Phase 4 labels

**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Phase:** 4 (gate G1)
**Affects:** reference.md §2.1, §2.4, §3.1, §4.3; `configs/problem.yaml`, `configs/labels.yaml`
**Reports:** `reports/label_source_comparison.md`, `reports/label_qa.md` (both generated by `uv run heatwave build-labels`)

All evidence uses **development years 1981–2020 only**. 2021–2025 is the single-use final test; choosing the label by looking at it would leak. NOAA station data for 2021+ was not even downloaded.

## 1. The normal: 6 harmonics

The first check on 3 harmonics showed apparent errors of about 1 °C at certain calendar days. An **out-of-sample** test fitted on alternate years 1991–2020 and scored on the others. It showed those were sampling noise shared across correlated districts, not shape error. All smoothings were within 0.02 °C RMSE (POWER: 6 harmonics 2.917, 3 harmonics 2.926, ±15-day window 2.921, raw daily means 2.977; IMD similar). **6 harmonics was best for both sources and is used.**

## 2. Neither POWER nor IMD can feed IMD's absolute thresholds as served

March–June, district level, POWER vs IMD 1° grid:
- POWER is **~3.1 °C warmer** than IMD (+2.7 in March–April, +3.5 in May–June). District-days ≥ 45 °C: POWER 41,646 vs IMD 2,470.
- Daily anomalies track well: median correlation 0.85.
- Heatwave flags agree poorly: full rule κ 0.30, departure-only κ 0.51.

The plan's decision table pointed to "POWER bias-corrected to IMD". That is only right if IMD's *level* is right. NOAA GSOD station daily maxima were used to check: 12 UP stations have data; only *reported* maxima are used, since hourly-derived ones are biased low. POWER runs **+1.8 to +2.7 °C warm** against stations and IMD **−0.4 to −2.3 °C cool**, worst on the hottest days.

## 3. Candidates scored against station heatwave days

At each station's grid cell, every candidate is scored against the station's own heatwave days (IMD's criteria are station-defined). Station-based maps are fitted leave-one-station-out. Final run, evaluation season March–July:

| Candidate | Fit stations (4): ratio / κ | Check stations (6, never fitted on): ratio / κ |
|---|---|---|
| POWER as-is | 3.08 / 0.37 | 2.65 / 0.38 |
| IMD as-is | 0.57 / 0.49 | 0.60 / 0.52 |
| POWER → IMD | 0.60 / 0.44 | 0.51 / 0.44 |
| POWER → stations (statewide map) | 1.05 / 0.45 | 0.75 / 0.49 |
| **POWER − spatial plane → stations (chosen)** | **1.02 / 0.48** | **0.88 / 0.53** |

**Fit stations:** Lucknow, Prayagraj, Bareilly and Gorakhpur, each with ≥ 10 seasons and ≥ 70 % reported maxima. **Check stations:** Agra, Varanasi, Jhansi, Meerut, Fursatganj and Bahraich, with ≥ 400 reported season days. Agra was not a fit station because only 18 % of its maxima are reported values; Varanasi has 8 good seasons, under the minimum of 10. The minimum was set before results and was not lowered to admit stations.

## 4. Why the spatial plane

The owner first chose the statewide station map. The out-of-sample check then showed it **over-cools Bundelkhand**. At Jhansi, raw POWER is only +0.4 °C warm, against about +2.3 °C elsewhere; after statewide correction it was −1.8 °C, with 19 days ≥ 45 °C against the station's 59. **IMD independently shows the same pattern:** POWER − IMD is 1.1 °C smaller over Bundelkhand (+2.10) than over the rest of UP (+3.19), with a north–south gradient (correlation with latitude 0.55). A plausible physical cause is irrigation, which cools the Ganga plains in reality but not in the reanalysis behind POWER.

Inverse-distance interpolation of station biases could not recover Jhansi (its neighbours all have large biases). A full hybrid (POWER → IMD locally, then IMD → stations) imported IMD's local errors (mean |bias| 0.67 °C). A **plane in latitude/longitude** of the district POWER − IMD bias keeps the regional gradient and discards IMD's local station-density artefacts. Removing it before the station map gave the best result on every measure (exploratory, leave-one-out, 10 stations): mean |bias| 0.36 vs 0.48 °C, hot-day bias 0.62 vs 0.73 °C, Jhansi ≥ 45 °C days 51 vs 19 (station 59). In the final committed scoring, Jhansi's heatwave-day κ is **0.80** (IMD 0.73).

Fitted plane (March–July, 1991–2020): POWER − IMD ≈ −20.40 + 0.514·lat + 0.114·lon °C, district residual RMSE 0.62 °C.

**Decision (owner, after the evidence above):** label Tmax = POWER district Tmax − plane, then monthly quantile map to station levels. Plane and map are **fitted once on 1991–2020 and are part of the label definition**, like the normal. The alternative, refitting per fold, would give every fold a different target and break live verification. The cost is a mild leak into validation years 2006–2020, of the same kind as the fixed normal. 2021–2025 stay out-of-sample.

Versions in this build: label `lbl_a0e4a4502fe6`, plane `pl_35f59da4afef`, map `qm_7256cb89609d`.

## 5. Evaluation season: March–July

Share of heatwave days by month:

| Month | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Jul | Aug |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stations' own heatwave days | 2.6 % | 5.6 % | 25.6 % | 49.0 % | **16.5 %** | 0.5 % |
| Label (statewide-map build) | 3.6 % | 7.7 % | 27.2 % | 41.6 % | 16.7 % | 2.5 % |
| IMD label | 2.7 % | 7.3 % | 18.3 % | 55.3 % | 16.1 % | 0.3 % |

July heat before a late monsoon onset is a genuine heatwave under IMD's rule. August exceeds 1 % only in our label, which is a label artifact. **Decision (owner): evaluate March–July; training rows 15 Feb – 15 Aug.** This deviates from a plain "> 1 % of label days" rule, which would also have included August. The final label's season check against stations passes (March–July).

## 6. Label QA (gate G1): pass

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Season shape vs stations | Stations > 1 % in March–July = evaluation season |
| Years vs stations' heatwave rate | correlation **0.80**; **5 of 8** top years shared (pass: ≥ 0.7 and ≥ 5) |
| Episodes (state-wide, ≥ 1 district) | **265** in development years (assumption A3, order 10², holds) |
| District spread | 3.1 (Shravasti) to 12.5 (Mahoba, Bundelkhand) heatwave days per season |
| Sensitivity labels, March–July | IMD label 0.57× the main count, κ 0.48; percentile label 0.68×, κ 0.47 |
| Plains criteria (A1) | Area-weighted district elevation 67–374 m: plains everywhere |
| Phase 3 follow-up (Sonbhadra edge cell) | On its three June flag dates, Sonbhadra's departure was −4.7, −2.1 and −9.6 °C; no label near a threshold |

**QA check changed after seeing its result, with the reason:** the original check, "known severe seasons rank in the top third", used an India-wide list. 2015 (Andhra/Telangana) and 2019 (mainly Bihar) ranked 24th and 23rd *at UP stations themselves*, so the list was wrong for UP, not the label. The check now uses the stations' own heatwave years. The original list and both rankings remain in `reports/label_qa.md`.

## Limitations carried forward

- Four fit stations and six check stations. Bundelkhand rests on Jhansi (5 seasons) plus IMD's pattern. More station data would strengthen the correction; added to To do later.
- Gorakhpur (north-east) under-counts under every corrected candidate. Over March–July the station has 145 heatwave days; the chosen label gives 71 (κ 0.38), the lowest of the corrected candidates, against 78–97 for the others. The plane makes the north-east slightly cooler. The cause is unexplained; the eastern humid regime is a candidate. Worth watching in the by-region results of Phase 6.
- The 1° IMD grid sets only the *large-scale* spatial adjustment, not local detail.
- Station points vs ~3,000 km² districts: κ around 0.5 is near the ceiling of what any gridded label can reach.
